answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether the work maps a meadow, models a plume, or grades quartz. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires $100,000 in separate bonds; funds cannot back two identities at once. This does not prove each agent has a different owner, but it makes a swarm expensive by tying up capital that the attacker could otherwise invest or spend.
